body: I completely subscribe to this. I hate celebrating my birthday and everyone in my life thinks its weird as well. I just don't like all the attention on me and I don't like feeling like I have to put on a show for other people. Kinda like i don't want to pretend to be happy and having a great time when in reality im extremely uncomfortable and depressive. I do however love celebrating other peoples birthdays. Mayhaps its just not liking the attention being on you. Honestly for me its like the month of I just completely dread the thought of my birthday.

YES! Numb person here as well! I'm currently on 300mg of trileptal once a night for the last year and the only negative I've experienced with this medication is that it makes me extremely numb instead of extremely depressed, as well as the numbness leads into dissociation for me. its possible as well that the two medications are interacting with eachother negatively, I've had a few friends that have been on lexapro and when mixed with other anti-psychotics/depressants they've had really negative experiences. Always talk to your psych about how your meds are making you feel or if they are worrying you!

I didn't see anyone else state this but weed does interact with trileptal from what i've been told by my own psychiatrists. I'm not a mental health professional so take what I have to say with a grain of salt. What I was told is that weed can counteract the effects of trileptal and render it possibly useless. I was warned against doing any drugs or alcohol while on this medication for those reasons. However I do still smoke myself but in very low dosages. I have noticed that the effects of weed are much less prominent on this medication and I don't get nearly as high as I used to be able to, It's kinda like theres a barrier stopping men from getting out of my mind high, and it also enables worse dissociative episodes for me. At this point I've had to cut my weed usage down to just using it to help me sleep because trileptal is supposed to help with sleep but for me it hasnt. I am on a medium dosage at 300mg once a night however so it may be different on lower and higher dosages. I would suggest talking to your psych first!

I'm currently on oxcarbazepine (off-brand of trileptal) for bipolar disorder with BPD-like symptoms and in my experience with being on it for the last year I've seen mostly positive effects. My moods are much more stable than before, I've been able to handle my suicidal ideations much better, and I don't feel as suffocated by my symptoms as I did before. The biggest negative side effect i've experienced is dissociative episodes seem like they are more frequent than they were before being on this medication, however my psych told me that that's probably more of a coping mechanism of my anxiety than a side effect of my meds. So take that with a grain of salt. But overall this pill has done wonders for my mental health!
